Drop-down 4 - No: Adding the Owner role changes nothing, because deny assignments take precedence over role assignments regardless of how privileged the role is. The only documented way to exempt an identity is the ExcludePrincipals property of the deny assignment, which the deployment stack populates from its excluded principals setting - and the scenario states there are none.
tags: azure rbac,deny assignments,deployment stacks,denydelete,inheritance,additive model,evaluation logic,effective permissions

sotto_argomento: Interpret access assignments
domanda: During an access review, an administrator examines a deny assignment that is listed on the Access control (IAM) page of an Azure subscription. Which three statements about deny assignments are true? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_a: A deny assignment can exempt specific security principals from the block by using the ExcludePrincipals property.
opzione_b: A deny assignment blocks the specified actions even when a role assignment grants the principal access to those actions.
opzione_c: A deny assignment can be prevented from being inherited by child scopes by setting DoNotApplyToChildScopes to true.
opzione_d: A deny assignment does not apply to a principal that is assigned the Owner role at the same scope.
opzione_e: A deny assignment can block only data plane actions (DataActions) and never control plane actions.
spiegazione: Correct: a. ExcludePrincipals is a documented deny assignment property: 'An array of Microsoft Entra principal object IDs (user, group, service principal, or managed identity) to which the deny assignment does not apply.' Excluding principals is listed as a capability that deny assignments have and role assignments do not. Correct: b. Microsoft Learn defines a deny assignment as attaching 'a set of deny actions to a user, group, or service principal at a particular scope for the purpose of denying access. Deny assignments block users from performing specific Azure resource actions even if a role assignment grants them access.' In the evaluation logic, Azure Resource Manager checks deny assignments first: 'If a deny assignment applies, access is blocked. Otherwise, evaluation continues.' Correct: c. DoNotApplyToChildScopes 'Specifies whether the deny assignment applies to child scopes. Default value is false,' and 'Prevent inheritance to child scopes' is listed as a deny assignment capability. Wrong: d. Owner is not exempt. Deny assignments are evaluated before role assignments and block access regardless of which role is assigned; the only documented exemption mechanism is ExcludePrincipals. Deny assignments even apply to classic subscription administrator assignments. Wrong: e. A deny assignment requires at least one Actions or one DataActions entry and supports Permissions.Actions and Permissions.NotActions for control plane actions as well as Permissions.DataActions and Permissions.NotDataActions for data plane actions. Deployment stack deny assignments, for example, deny the control plane action */delete.

sotto_argomento: Interpret access assignments
domanda:
Adventure Works has a management group named mg-adventureworks that contains a subscription named sub-prod. The sub-prod subscription contains a resource group named rg-finance. A user named Sam is assigned the Contributor role at the mg-adventureworks scope and the Reader role at the rg-finance scope. There are no deny assignments and no role assignment conditions. For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
1. Sam can create a storage account in rg-finance.
2. The Reader role assignment at rg-finance reduces Sam's effective permissions in rg-finance to read-only.
3. Sam can assign the Reader role to another user at the sub-prod scope.
opzione_a: Sam can create a storage account in rg-finance.
opzione_b: The Reader role assignment at rg-finance reduces Sam's effective permissions in rg-finance to read-only.
opzione_c: Sam can assign the Reader role to another user at the sub-prod scope.
spiegazione: Statement 1 - Yes: Scopes are structured in a parent-child relationship and 'Lower levels inherit role permissions from higher levels.' The Contributor assignment at mg-adventureworks therefore inherits to sub-prod and to rg-finance. Contributor's Actions are * (create and manage resources of all types), so Sam can create a storage account in rg-finance. Statement 2 - No: Azure RBAC is an additive model, so effective permissions are the sum of the role assignments, not the intersection. Microsoft Learn uses this exact example: a user granted Contributor at subscription scope and Reader on a resource group has 'effectively the Contributor role for the subscription. Therefore, in this case, the Reader role assignment has no impact.' A lower-scope Reader assignment cannot subtract permissions granted at a higher scope; only a deny assignment blocks access that a role assignment grants. Statement 3 - No: Contributor 'Grants full access to manage all resources, but does not allow you to assign roles in Azure RBAC.' Its NotActions include Microsoft.Authorization/*/Write and Microsoft.Authorization/*/Delete, which subtract Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write from the * in Actions. Reader grants only read access and adds nothing here, so Sam has no effective permission to create a role assignment at sub-prod.

sotto_argomento: Interpret access assignments
domanda: A custom role named VM Operations has its Actions property set to Microsoft.Compute/* and its NotActions property set to Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/delete. A user named Dana is assigned the VM Operations custom role at the scope of a resource group named rg-app01. Dana is also assigned the built-in Virtual Machine Contributor role at the rg-app01 scope. No deny assignments exist. Dana attempts to delete a virtual machine in rg-app01. What is the result, and why?
opzione_a: The deletion succeeds, because Azure RBAC is an additive model and NotActions is not a deny rule.
opzione_b: The deletion fails, because a NotActions entry in any assigned role removes that action from the user's effective permissions across all role assignments.
opzione_c: The deletion fails, because when two roles are assigned at the same scope, the more restrictive role definition takes precedence.
opzione_d: The deletion succeeds only if Dana is additionally assigned the Owner role at the subscription scope.
spiegazione: Correct: a. Microsoft Learn states 'Azure RBAC is an additive model, so your effective permissions are the sum of your role assignments,' and specifically notes that 'If a user is assigned a role that excludes an action in NotActions, and is assigned a second role that grants access to the same action, the user is allowed to perform that action. NotActions is not a deny rule.' The Virtual Machine Contributor assignment independently grants the delete action, so Dana can delete the VM. Wrong: b. NotActions is scoped to the single role definition it belongs to: effective permissions for that role are computed as Actions - NotActions. It does not subtract the action from other role assignments. Wrong: c. Azure RBAC has no 'most restrictive wins' precedence between role assignments. Only deny assignments block access that a role assignment grants, and Azure Resource Manager evaluates deny assignments before narrowing role assignments. Wrong: d. Owner at the subscription scope is unnecessary. The existing Virtual Machine Contributor assignment at rg-app01 already includes the delete action, and adding a broader assignment is not a prerequisite for the additive model to apply.
tags: azure rbac,notactions,custom role,additive model,effective permissions,virtual machine contributor

sotto_argomento: Interpret access assignments
domanda: While reviewing the Access control (IAM) page of a resource group, an administrator opens the Deny assignments tab and finds an entry that nobody on the team remembers creating. The administrator now wants to apply an equivalent deny assignment to a second resource group. Which statement correctly describes how deny assignments are created?
opzione_a: You can't directly create deny assignments; they're created and managed by Azure, although specifying deny settings when you create a deployment stack causes Azure to create one.
opzione_b: On the Access control (IAM) page, select Add and then select Add deny assignment, and choose the principal and the actions to deny.
opzione_c: Run the New-AzDenyAssignment cmdlet in Az PowerShell and specify the principal, the denied actions, and the scope.
opzione_d: Add the actions you want to block to the NotActions property of a custom role definition, then assign that custom role at the target scope.
spiegazione: Correct: a. Microsoft Learn states explicitly that 'You can't directly create your own deny assignments. Deny assignments are created and managed by Azure.' The documented way to cause one to exist is to specify deny settings when creating a deployment stack, which creates a deny assignment owned by the deployment stack resources. All deny assignments are currently system protected (IsSystemProtected is Yes in all cases). Wrong: b. There is no Add deny assignment action in Access control (IAM). The Deny assignments tab is read-only and only lists deny assignments at or inherited to the scope; viewing requires Microsoft.Authorization/denyAssignments/read. Wrong: c. Az PowerShell exposes Get-AzDenyAssignment for listing deny assignments, but there is no supported cmdlet to create one, because creation is reserved to Azure. Wrong: d. NotActions is not a deny rule. Microsoft Learn states 'NotActions is not a deny rule - it is simply a convenient way to create a set of allowed actions when specific actions need to be excluded.' If a second role assignment grants the same action, the user can still perform it, so NotActions cannot replicate a deny assignment.
tags: azure rbac,deny assignments,deployment stacks,system protected,access control iam

sotto_argomento: Interpret access assignments
domanda: The following strings are Azure RBAC scopes taken from a role assignment audit. Arrange the five scopes in order from the broadest (least specific) scope to the most specific scope.
opzione_a: /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/Example-Storage-rg
opzione_b: /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/marketing-group
opzione_c: /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/Example-Storage-rg/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/azurestorage12345/blobServices/default/containers/blob-container-01
opzione_d: /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}
opzione_e: /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/Example-Storage-rg/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/azurestorage12345
spiegazione: Correct order: b, d, a, e, c. Microsoft Learn states that scopes are structured in a parent-child relationship and that 'Each level of hierarchy makes the scope more specific,' with management groups having 'the broadest (least specific) scope.' Option b is a management group scope, which uses the /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/{managementGroupName} format and sits above subscriptions. Option d is the subscription scope. Option a adds /resourceGroups/{name}, narrowing to a resource group inside that subscription. Option e adds /providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/{name}, narrowing to a single storage account resource in that resource group. Option c is the narrowest: it extends the storage account scope with /blobServices/default/containers/blob-container-01, targeting one blob container (a child resource). Any other ordering contradicts the documented hierarchy, because each additional identifier separated by the slash (/) character makes the scope more specific, and lower levels inherit role permissions from higher levels.

sotto_argomento: Interpret access assignments
domanda: User5 is assigned the Virtual Machine Contributor role at the scope of a resource group named RG-VMs. RG-VMs contains a virtual machine named VM1. User5 reports that an attempt to delete VM1 fails with an authorization error. Which of the following could explain the failure? Select all that apply.
opzione_a: A CanNotDelete (Delete) management lock is applied to VM1 or is inherited from RG-VMs or the subscription.
opzione_b: A deny assignment that includes a matching delete action applies at the scope of VM1.
opzione_c: The Virtual Machine Contributor role definition does not include the 'Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/delete' action.
opzione_d: A different role that is also assigned to User5 lists 'Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/delete' in its NotActions, which subtracts the action from User5's effective permissions.
opzione_e: The role assignment was created only a few minutes ago, the change has not yet taken effect, and User5 has not signed out and signed back in.
spiegazione: Correct answers (a, b, e). (a) is a valid cause: management locks are independent of Azure RBAC. Microsoft Learn states that a lock 'overrides any user permissions' and that 'unlike with role-based access control (RBAC), you use management locks to apply a restriction across all users and roles.' CanNotDelete means authorized users can read and modify a resource but cannot delete it, and locks are inherited, so a lock at RG-VMs or the subscription reaches VM1; the most restrictive lock in the inheritance chain takes precedence. (b) is a valid cause: deny assignments 'block users from performing specific Azure resource actions even if a role assignment grants them access,' and they are evaluated before role assignments. (e) is a valid cause: the docs note that 'when you assign roles or remove role assignments, it can take up to 10 minutes for changes to take effect,' that Azure Resource Manager caches configurations, and that signing out and signing back in forces a refresh of role assignment changes. (c) is false: Virtual Machine Contributor does include the virtual machine delete action. Its documented description is 'Lets you manage virtual machines, but not access to them, and not the virtual network or storage account they're connected to,' and managing virtual machines includes deleting them; the role's genuine gaps are the connected virtual network and storage account, and access to the data inside the VM. (d) is false because it repeats the classic NotActions misconception. Microsoft Learn is explicit that 'NotActions is not a deny rule' and that a user assigned a role excluding an action in NotActions who is also assigned a second role granting that action is allowed to perform it. NotActions is subtracted only within the role definition that declares it, so it can never remove an action that Virtual Machine Contributor grants.
tags: azure rbac,troubleshooting,resource lock,cannotdelete,deny assignment,notactions,virtual machine contributor,replication delay

sotto_argomento: Interpret access assignments
domanda: Your organization is documenting how Azure evaluates access to resources. Which statements about Azure deny assignments are true? Select all that apply.
opzione_a: Deny assignments are evaluated before role assignments, so a matching deny assignment blocks an action even when a role assignment grants that action.
opzione_b: An administrator who holds the Owner role at subscription scope can create a deny assignment directly from the Access control (IAM) page in the Azure portal.
opzione_c: A deny assignment can exempt specific security principals from the block by using the ExcludePrincipals property.
opzione_d: A deny assignment can be prevented from applying to child scopes by setting the DoNotApplyToChildScopes property to true.
opzione_e: Deny assignments and the NotActions property of a role definition are two names for the same enforcement mechanism.
spiegazione: Correct answers (a, c, d). (a) is true: the documented Azure RBAC evaluation sequence retrieves all role assignments and deny assignments that apply to the resource, and then 'if a deny assignment applies, access is blocked. Otherwise, evaluation continues.' Deny assignments therefore short-circuit evaluation before any role assignment is considered. (c) is true: ExcludePrincipals is a documented deny assignment property holding 'an array of Microsoft Entra principal object IDs (user, group, service principal, or managed identity) to which the deny assignment does not apply.' It is commonly combined with the All Principals system-defined principal to deny everyone except a small set of accounts. (d) is true: DoNotApplyToChildScopes is a documented Boolean property that 'specifies whether the deny assignment applies to child scopes,' with a default value of false, meaning that by default a deny assignment is inherited by child scopes. Preventing inheritance to child scopes is listed in the docs as a capability of deny assignments that role assignments do not have. (b) is false: Microsoft Learn states explicitly, 'You can't directly create your own deny assignments. Deny assignments are created and managed by Azure.' They arise indirectly, for example from deny settings on a deployment stack or from Azure managed applications, and all deny assignments currently have IsSystemProtected set to true. No Azure role, including Owner, changes this. (e) is false: the docs contain a dedicated section titled 'Differences between NotActions and deny assignments' clarifying that they 'are not the same and serve different purposes.' NotActions is only a convenient way to subtract specific actions from a wildcard Actions entry within a single role definition, whereas a deny assignment is an actual block that overrides granted access.

sotto_argomento: Interpret access assignments
domanda: Case study: Fabrikam, Inc. uses a single Azure subscription named Sub1 that contains a resource group named RG-Finance. RG-Finance contains a storage account named safinance. A Microsoft Entra group named FinanceAdmins is assigned the Contributor role at the scope of Sub1. A user named User10 is a member of FinanceAdmins and is also assigned the Reader role directly at the scope of RG-Finance. A new business requirement states that User10 must be able to grant a colleague the Storage Blob Data Reader role on safinance. When User10 opens the Access control (IAM) page for safinance, the Add > Add role assignment option is disabled. You must resolve this while granting User10 the least privilege necessary. What should you do?
opzione_a: Assign User10 the Owner role at the scope of RG-Finance.
opzione_b: Assign User10 the Role Based Access Control Administrator role at the scope of safinance.
opzione_c: Remove the Reader role assignment at the scope of RG-Finance, because it is overriding the Contributor permissions that User10 inherits from FinanceAdmins.
opzione_d: Assign User10 the Global Administrator role in Microsoft Entra ID.
spiegazione: Correct answer (b): The documented cause of a disabled Add role assignment option is that 'you're currently signed in with a user that doesn't have permission to assign roles at the selected scope,' and the documented solution is to be assigned a role that has the 'Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write' permission, 'such as Role Based Access Control Administrator, at the scope you're trying to assign the role.' User10's inherited Contributor role cannot assign roles because the Contributor role definition lists 'Microsoft.Authorization/*/Write' in its NotActions, and effective permissions are Actions minus NotActions. Role Based Access Control Administrator is described as letting you 'manage user access to Azure resources' and 'assign roles in Azure RBAC' without granting broad resource management, and assigning it at the storage account scope is the narrowest scope that satisfies the requirement. (a) would technically work, because Owner has a wildcard Actions and no NotActions, but it grants full management of every resource in RG-Finance on top of role assignment rights, so it violates the least-privilege requirement stated in the scenario. (c) is wrong because it misstates how Azure RBAC combines assignments: the model is additive and the effective permissions are the sum of the role assignments, so a Reader assignment never overrides or suppresses an inherited Contributor assignment. Removing it changes nothing, and User10 would still be unable to assign roles. (d) is wrong because Microsoft Entra roles and Azure roles are separate systems; by default a Global Administrator has no access to Azure resources at all, so this neither addresses the problem directly nor respects least privilege.
tags: azure rbac,troubleshooting,role based access control administrator,contributor,notactions,least privilege,role assignment

sotto_argomento: Interpret access assignments
domanda: A management group named MG1 contains an Azure subscription named Sub1. Sub1 contains two resource groups named RG1 and RG2. A user named User9 is assigned the Owner role at the scope of MG1. An Azure managed application deployment caused Azure to create a deny assignment at the scope of RG1 with the following configuration: Actions contains '*/write'; Principals contains the All Principals system-defined principal; ExcludePrincipals is empty; DoNotApplyToChildScopes is set to false; IsSystemProtected is set to true. Evaluate the following three statements: (1) User9 can create a new virtual machine in RG1. (2) User9 can create a new virtual machine in RG2. (3) User9 can delete the deny assignment from RG1 by using the Azure portal.
opzione_a: User9 can create a new virtual machine in RG1.
opzione_b: User9 can create a new virtual machine in RG2.
opzione_c: User9 can delete the deny assignment from RG1 by using the Azure portal.
spiegazione: Statement 1 - No: creating a virtual machine requires write actions, which the deny assignment blocks via '*/write' for the All Principals system-defined principal with no exclusions. Deny assignments 'block users from performing specific Azure resource actions even if a role assignment grants them access,' and in the documented evaluation sequence Azure Resource Manager checks deny assignments before role assignments: 'if a deny assignment applies, access is blocked. Otherwise, evaluation continues.' User9's Owner role at MG1 is inherited down to RG1 but is irrelevant because evaluation never reaches the role assignments. Statement 2 - Yes: the deny assignment is scoped to RG1. Scopes are structured in a parent-child relationship, and inheritance flows only from parent to child, so a deny assignment at RG1 does not reach the sibling resource group RG2. Note that DoNotApplyToChildScopes is set to false here, which means the deny assignment is inherited by RG1's child scopes - but RG2 is not a child of RG1. User9's Owner role at MG1 is inherited by Sub1 and therefore by RG2, so the creation succeeds. Statement 3 - No: IsSystemProtected is set to true. Microsoft Learn defines this property as specifying 'whether this deny assignment was created by Azure and cannot be edited or deleted,' and notes that 'currently, all deny assignments are system protected.' The docs also state plainly that 'you can't directly create your own deny assignments. Deny assignments are created and managed by Azure.' No Azure role, including Owner, allows User9 to remove it; the correct approach is to remove the underlying managed application.
tags: azure rbac,deny assignment,management group,scope inheritance,owner,issystemprotected,managed application,all principals

sotto_argomento: Interpret access assignments
domanda: A deployment stack protects a storage account named sa-stack. As a result, Azure created a deny assignment at the scope of sa-stack with the following configuration: Actions contains '*/delete'; Principals contains the All Principals system-defined principal; ExcludePrincipals contains the object ID of a user named User3; DoNotApplyToChildScopes is set to true. A user named User3 and a user named User4 are both assigned the Contributor role at the scope of the resource group that contains sa-stack. Which statement correctly describes the outcome?
opzione_a: Both User3 and User4 can delete sa-stack, because a Contributor role assignment at the resource group scope is inherited by sa-stack.
opzione_b: User3 can delete sa-stack, but User4 cannot.
opzione_c: Neither User3 nor User4 can delete sa-stack, because a deny assignment that uses All Principals applies to every principal in the directory regardless of any exclusions.
opzione_d: User4 can delete sa-stack, but User3 cannot, because ExcludePrincipals lists the principals that the deny assignment applies to.
spiegazione: Correct answer (b): The deny assignment blocks '*/delete' for the All Principals system-defined principal, which 'represents all users, groups, service principals, and managed identities in a Microsoft Entra directory.' Because deny assignments are evaluated before role assignments and block access 'even if a role assignment grants them access,' User4's Contributor role does not permit the deletion. However, ExcludePrincipals holds 'an array of Microsoft Entra principal object IDs ... to which the deny assignment does not apply,' and the docs note that 'All Principals can be combined with ExcludePrincipals to deny all principals except some users.' User3 is excluded, so the deny assignment does not apply to User3, evaluation continues to the role assignments, and User3's inherited Contributor role grants the delete. (a) is wrong because although the Contributor inheritance claim is true on its own, it ignores the deny assignment, which is evaluated first and blocks User4. (c) is wrong because it contradicts the documented purpose of ExcludePrincipals; the exclusion is honored, and combining All Principals with ExcludePrincipals is the standard documented pattern. (d) is wrong because it inverts the semantics of the two properties: Principals lists who the deny assignment applies to, and ExcludePrincipals lists who is exempt from it. Note that DoNotApplyToChildScopes set to true only stops the deny assignment from reaching child scopes such as blob containers; it has no bearing on sa-stack itself, which is the scope of the deny assignment.

sotto_argomento: Interpret access assignments
domanda: User6 is assigned the Reader role at the scope of an Azure subscription named Sub1. User6 is also assigned the Contributor role at the scope of a resource group named RG1, which is in Sub1. Sub1 also contains a second resource group named RG2, on which User6 has no direct role assignment. A management lock with the CanNotDelete (Delete) lock level is applied to RG1. Select the answer choice that completes each statement based on the information presented.
opzione_a: User6 can create a new storage account in RG1: [Yes | No]
opzione_b: User6 can delete an existing storage account in RG1: [Yes | No]
opzione_c: User6 can assign the Reader role to another user at the scope of RG1: [Yes | No]
opzione_d: User6 can delete an existing storage account in RG2: [Yes | No]
spiegazione: Statement 1 - Yes: at RG1 the effective permissions are the sum of the inherited Reader assignment and the direct Contributor assignment, which equals Contributor. Contributor has Actions set to the wildcard '*', which permits creating resources. The CanNotDelete lock does not interfere, because the docs state that 'CanNotDelete means authorized users can read and modify a resource, but they can't delete it' - create and modify remain allowed. Statement 2 - No: the CanNotDelete lock applied at RG1 is inherited by all resources in RG1, including resources added later, and the lock 'overrides any user permissions.' Locks apply across all users and roles regardless of RBAC, so Contributor does not help. Statement 3 - No: assigning a role requires the 'Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write' action. The Contributor role definition lists 'Microsoft.Authorization/*/Write' and 'Microsoft.Authorization/*/Delete' in its NotActions, and effective permissions are computed as Actions minus NotActions, so this action is subtracted. Reader does not grant it either. User6 would need Role Based Access Control Administrator, User Access Administrator, or Owner. Statement 4 - No: the only assignment that reaches RG2 is the Reader role inherited from Sub1, which grants view-only access. The Contributor assignment is scoped to RG1 and is not inherited sideways to a sibling resource group, because scopes are structured in a parent-child relationship and only lower levels inherit from higher levels.

sotto_argomento: Interpret access assignments
domanda: An administrator named Admin1 is assigned the Owner role at the scope of an Azure subscription named Sub1. Sub1 contains a storage account named sa1. Admin1 signs in to the Azure portal with their Microsoft Entra account, opens a blob container in sa1, sets the authentication method to Microsoft Entra User Account, and receives an authorization error when attempting to list the blobs. There are no deny assignments, locks, or network restrictions in place. What is the most likely explanation?
opzione_a: The Owner role definition lists the Microsoft.Storage resource provider in its NotActions.
opzione_b: The Owner role grants control plane access through a wildcard Actions entry, but the role definition contains no DataActions, so it does not grant access to blob data.
opzione_c: Owner role assignments made at subscription scope are not inherited by storage accounts in child resource groups.
opzione_d: Blob data access requires the role assignment to be made at the container scope; Azure ignores data access granted at subscription scope.
spiegazione: Correct answer (b): Azure RBAC deliberately separates the control plane from the data plane. Control plane permissions come from Actions and NotActions; data plane permissions come from DataActions and NotDataActions. Microsoft Learn explains that this separation 'prevents roles with wildcards (*) from having unrestricted access to your data' and gives this exact scenario: a user with the Owner role at subscription scope has a wildcard action that inherits down and lets them perform all control plane actions such as reading, writing, and deleting containers, 'However, Alice cannot perform data plane actions without taking additional steps. For example, by default, Alice cannot read the blobs inside a container.' The Owner role has Actions set to '*' and no DataActions. The fix is to assign a role that includes blob DataActions, such as Storage Blob Data Reader or Storage Blob Data Contributor, or to authenticate with the storage account access key instead. (a) is wrong because the Owner role's NotActions is empty; it is the absence of DataActions, not an exclusion, that causes this. (c) is wrong because role assignments are inherited by child scopes; the Owner assignment absolutely does reach sa1, which is why Admin1 can still see and manage the storage account resource itself. (d) is wrong because a role with blob DataActions works when assigned at subscription, resource group, storage account, or container scope; Azure does not ignore data access granted at higher scopes.
tags: azure rbac,dataactions,control plane,data plane,owner,storage blob data reader,troubleshooting

sotto_argomento: Interpret access assignments
domanda: A user who is assigned the Global Administrator role in Microsoft Entra ID reports that no Azure subscriptions appear on the Subscriptions page of the Azure portal, and that they cannot view the Access control (IAM) page for any management group. The tenant contains several active subscriptions. You must enable this user to regain access management over all subscriptions in the tenant. What should you do?
opzione_a: Assign the user the User Administrator role in Microsoft Entra ID.
opzione_b: In Microsoft Entra ID, turn on the 'Access management for Azure resources' toggle to elevate the user's access.
opzione_c: Assign the user the Contributor role in Microsoft Entra ID under Roles and administrators.
opzione_d: Add the user as a Co-Administrator on each subscription.
spiegazione: Correct answer (b): By default, Azure roles and Microsoft Entra roles do not span both systems. Microsoft Learn states, 'by default, the Global Administrator doesn't have access to Azure resources.' The documented remedy is elevation: 'if a Global Administrator elevates their access by choosing the Access management for Azure resources switch in the Azure portal, the Global Administrator will be granted the User Access Administrator role (an Azure role) on all subscriptions for a particular tenant.' The docs note this 'switch can be helpful to regain access to a subscription,' which is exactly this scenario. As a best practice the elevation should be removed once the necessary role assignments have been made. (a) is wrong because User Administrator is another Microsoft Entra role that manages users and groups in the directory; it confers no permissions over Azure resources, so it reproduces the original problem. (c) is wrong because Contributor is an Azure role, not a Microsoft Entra role, and it cannot be assigned on the Roles and administrators page; Azure roles are assigned on the Access control (IAM) page of a management group, subscription, resource group, or resource. (d) is wrong because the classic subscription administrator roles, including Co-Administrator, are fully retired: they were retired and unsupported as of August 31, 2024, and as of May 2026 you must use Azure RBAC to manage access.
tags: microsoft entra id,global administrator,elevate access,user access administrator,azure roles vs entra roles,troubleshooting

sotto_argomento: Interpret access assignments
domanda: A service principal named SP1 is assigned the Owner role at the scope of a resource group named RG-Prod. Azure has also applied a deny assignment at the scope of RG-Prod. The deny assignment specifies the '*/delete' action and applies to all principals, with no excluded principals. SP1 attempts to delete a storage account in RG-Prod. What is the result?
opzione_a: The delete operation succeeds, because a role assignment that grants the Owner role always takes precedence over a deny assignment.
opzione_b: The delete operation is blocked, because deny assignments are evaluated before role assignments and block access even when a role assignment grants it.
opzione_c: The delete operation succeeds, because deny assignments apply only to users and groups, not to service principals.
opzione_d: The delete operation is blocked only if SP1 also lacks the 'Microsoft.Authorization/denyAssignments/write' permission to remove the deny assignment first.
spiegazione: Correct answer (b): Deny assignments take precedence over role assignments. Microsoft Learn defines a deny assignment as attaching 'a set of deny actions to a user, group, or service principal at a particular scope for the purpose of denying access' and states that deny assignments 'block users from performing specific Azure resource actions even if a role assignment grants them access.' The documented evaluation sequence confirms the ordering: Azure Resource Manager retrieves all role assignments and deny assignments that apply to the resource, and 'if a deny assignment applies, access is blocked. Otherwise, evaluation continues' to the role assignments. Because the deny assignment covers '*/delete' and applies to all principals, SP1's Owner role does not help. (a) is wrong because it reverses the documented precedence; no built-in role, including Owner, overrides a deny assignment. (c) is wrong because the Principals property of a deny assignment accepts object IDs of users, groups, service principals, and managed identities, and the system-defined 'All Principals' principal represents every one of those object types in the directory. (d) is wrong on two counts: the block is unconditional, and deny assignments cannot be removed this way at all because currently all deny assignments have IsSystemProtected set to true, meaning they were created by Azure and cannot be edited or deleted.

sotto_argomento: Interpret access assignments
domanda: A user named User1 is assigned the Reader role at the scope of an Azure subscription named Sub1. User1 is also assigned the Contributor role at the scope of a resource group named RG1, which is in Sub1. RG1 contains a virtual machine named VM1. What are User1's effective permissions on VM1?
opzione_a: User1 can view VM1 but cannot modify it, because the Reader assignment at the broader scope takes precedence over the Contributor assignment.
opzione_b: User1 can create and manage VM1, but cannot assign roles on VM1.
opzione_c: User1 can create and manage VM1 and can assign roles on VM1.
opzione_d: User1 has no effective access to VM1, because the two role assignments conflict and cancel each other out.
spiegazione: Correct answer (b): Azure RBAC is an additive model. As the Azure RBAC overview states, 'your effective permissions are the sum of your role assignments.' At the scope of RG1, User1 holds both Reader (inherited from Sub1) and Contributor (assigned directly), and the sum of those two is effectively Contributor. The Contributor role has Actions set to the wildcard '*', so it grants full management of VM1, but its NotActions include 'Microsoft.Authorization/*/Write' and 'Microsoft.Authorization/*/Delete', which subtract the ability to create or delete role assignments. Therefore User1 can manage VM1 but cannot assign roles on it. (a) is wrong because it inverts the model: a role assignment at a broader scope never overrides or limits a role assignment at a narrower scope; RBAC has no concept of a more-specific assignment losing to a less-specific one, and nothing about Reader subtracts from Contributor. (c) is wrong because assigning roles requires 'Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write', which Contributor explicitly excludes via NotActions; a role such as Role Based Access Control Administrator, User Access Administrator, or Owner would be required. (d) is wrong because overlapping role assignments never cancel out or produce a conflict in Azure RBAC; only a deny assignment can block access that a role assignment grants.
tags: azure rbac,role assignment,effective permissions,additive model,contributor,reader,scope inheritance

sotto_argomento: Interpret access assignments
domanda: Your Microsoft Entra tenant contains a group named Group1 and a group named Group2. Group2 is a member of Group1. A user named User8 is a member of Group2. Group1 is assigned the Contributor role at the scope of an Azure subscription named Sub1, which contains a resource group named RG1. There are no deny assignments or management locks. Evaluate the following three statements: (1) User8 has Contributor permissions on Sub1, because role assignments are transitive for groups. (2) If User8 is additionally assigned the Reader role directly at the scope of RG1, User8's effective permissions on resources in RG1 are reduced to read-only. (3) If you assign User8 the Reader role directly at the scope of Sub1, the Contributor access that User8 receives through Group1 is removed.
opzione_a: User8 has Contributor permissions on Sub1, because role assignments are transitive for groups.
opzione_b: If User8 is additionally assigned the Reader role directly at the scope of RG1, User8's effective permissions on resources in RG1 are reduced to read-only.
opzione_c: If you assign User8 the Reader role directly at the scope of Sub1, the Contributor access that User8 receives through Group1 is removed.
spiegazione: Statement 1 - Yes: Microsoft Learn states that 'role assignments are transitive for groups, which means that if a user is a member of a group and that group is a member of another group that has a role assignment, the user has the permissions in the role assignment.' User8 is a member of Group2, Group2 is a member of Group1, and Group1 holds the Contributor role on Sub1, so User8 has Contributor permissions on Sub1. The token acquired for Azure Resource Manager 'includes the user's group memberships (including transitive group memberships).' Statement 2 - No: this is the classic misreading of the additive model. Azure RBAC computes effective permissions as the sum of all role assignments, so at RG1 User8 would hold Contributor (inherited from Sub1 via nested group membership) plus Reader (direct), and the sum is still Contributor. Adding a less privileged role never subtracts privileges; the Reader assignment simply has no impact. Only a deny assignment can block access that a role assignment grants. Statement 3 - No: for the same reason. Adding a Reader assignment does not remove or replace the Contributor access granted through Group1. To reduce User8's access you must remove the source of the Contributor permissions - for example, remove User8 from Group2, remove Group2 from Group1, or change the role assigned to Group1.

sotto_argomento: Manage external users
domanda: Fabrikam Inc. is a partner organization with its own Microsoft Entra tenant. Contoso must give 200 Fabrikam employees access to a Contoso line-of-business application. The Fabrikam employees must sign in with their existing Fabrikam credentials, and each must receive an invitation email. A Contoso administrator has a CSV file that lists the 200 email addresses. Which action should the administrator perform?
opzione_a: In Microsoft Entra ID, go to Users > Bulk create and upload the CSV file.
opzione_b: In Microsoft Entra ID, go to Users > Bulk operations > Bulk invite and upload the CSV file.
opzione_c: Open the target group, select Members > Bulk operations > Import members, and upload the CSV file.
opzione_d: In Microsoft Entra ID, go to Users > Bulk create, upload the CSV file, and then change the UserType of each new account to Guest.
spiegazione: Correct (b): Bulk invite (Users > Bulk operations > Bulk invite) is the documented way to invite external B2B collaboration users from a CSV file and send them invitation emails. The template requires the Email address to invite [inviteeEmail] and Redirection url columns. Invited B2B users authenticate with credentials from their home identity provider, are created with UserType set to Guest, and receive a UPN in the form emailaddress#EXT#@domain. Wrong (a): Microsoft Learn explicitly states that the bulk create operation creates internal member accounts with the passwords specified in the CSV file and that no invitation emails are sent; the users would sign in with Contoso credentials, not Fabrikam credentials. Wrong (c): Bulk import members only adds objects that already exist in the directory to a group, referenced by object ID or UPN. It does not create or invite any user. Wrong (d): Changing UserType to Guest only changes the user's stated relationship to the organization and has no relation to how the user signs in, so these accounts would still be internal accounts with Contoso credentials and no invitation would be sent. Correction: option (b) previously read "Users > Bulk invite"; the documented navigation is Users > Bulk operations > Bulk invite, and the option text has been corrected to match the portal.
tags: microsoft entra id,b2b collaboration,bulk invite,guest users,usertype,external identities

sotto_argomento: Manage external users
domanda:
Adventure Works collaborates with two partner organizations that use the domains fabrikam.com and litware.com. You must configure the external collaboration settings of the Microsoft Entra tenant to meet the following requirements:
- Guest users must be able to see only their own profile information. They must not be able to see other users, groups, or group memberships.
- Only users who hold the User Administrator or Guest Inviter role may send B2B collaboration invitations.
- Invitations may be sent only to fabrikam.com and litware.com. Invitations to every other domain must fail.
Select the appropriate option for each setting.
opzione_a: Guest user access: [Guest users have the same access as members (most inclusive) | Guest users have limited access to properties and memberships of directory objects | Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects (most restrictive)]
opzione_b: Guest invite settings: [Anyone in the organization can invite guest users including guests and non-admins (most inclusive) | Member users and users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users including guests with member permissions | Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users | No one in the organization can invite guest users including admins (most restrictive)]
opzione_c: Collaboration restrictions: [Allow invitations to be sent to any domain (most inclusive) | Deny invitations to the specified domains | Allow invitations only to the specified domains (most restrictive)]
risposta_corretta: Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects (most restrictive),Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users,Allow invitations only to the specified domains (most restrictive)
spiegazione: Correct: (1) "Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects (most restrictive)" is the only level where guests can access only their own profiles and are not allowed to see other users' profiles, groups, or group memberships. "Same access as members" gives guests member-equivalent directory access, and the default "limited access" still lets guests see the membership of all non-hidden groups and read basic properties of other users. (2) "Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users" is documented as allowing only those users with the User Administrator or Guest Inviter role to invite guests. The "Anyone in the organization" option would let guests and non-admins invite; "Member users and users assigned to specific admin roles" would still let all member users invite; "No one in the organization" would block everyone including admins, so no invitations could be sent at all. (3) "Allow invitations only to the specified domains (most restrictive)" creates an allow list, so only the listed target domains can receive invitations and invitations to every other domain fail with a blocked-domain message. "Allow invitations to be sent to any domain" is the default and imposes no restriction; "Deny invitations to the specified domains" is a block list, which would require listing every domain in the world except the two partners. Remember you can create either an allow list or a block list, but not both, and only one policy per organization is supported. Note this list is checked at invitation time and does not apply to guests who already redeemed an invitation.
tags: external collaboration settings,guest user access,guest invite settings,collaboration restrictions,allow list,b2b

sotto_argomento: Manage external users
domanda: To satisfy a compliance requirement, you change Guest user access in the external collaboration settings of your Microsoft Entra tenant to "Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects (most restrictive)". A B2B collaboration guest user named Ben is affected by the change and holds no directory role. Which actions can Ben still perform by default? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_a: Change his own password
opzione_b: Enumerate the list of all users in the directory
opzione_c: Invite other guest users, if the Guest invite settings allow it
opzione_d: Read the display name and email address of other users in the directory
opzione_e: Manage his own mobile phone number
spiegazione: Correct: The "Restricted guest user permissions" column of the member/guest comparison table on Microsoft Learn lists exactly four Users and contacts capabilities: read their own properties, invite other guests if allowed by Guest invite settings, change their own password, and manage their own mobile phone number. That confirms A, C and E. B is wrong: enumerating the list of all users and contacts is a member user permission only; it is absent from both the default guest and the restricted guest columns. D is wrong: reading the display name, email, sign-in name, photo, user principal name, and user type of other users belongs to the DEFAULT guest permission set ("limited access"), but the most restrictive setting removes it - access to other users is no longer allowed even when searching by user principal name, object ID, or display name. Note that guests can still be added to administrator roles regardless of this setting, which would grant them broader access. Correction: the explanation previously claimed that "guests cannot enumerate the directory at any guest access level", which is not accurate - if Guest user access is set to "Guest users have the same access as members (most inclusive)", guests receive member permissions, which do include enumerating users and groups. The claim is true only for the default and restricted levels.
tags: guest permissions,restricted guest access,default user permissions,b2b collaboration,external collaboration settings

sotto_argomento: Manage external users
domanda:
In the external collaboration settings of the Microsoft Entra tenant for Woodgrove Bank, Collaboration restrictions is currently set to "Deny invitations to the specified domains" and fabrikam.com is listed as a target domain. Several guest users from other domains have already redeemed their invitations. Evaluate whether each of the following statements is true.
1. While the deny list is in place, you can also configure an allow list that contains contoso.com so that invitations to contoso.com are explicitly permitted.
2. If you switch the setting to "Allow invitations only to the specified domains (most restrictive)", the existing deny list configuration is discarded.
3. The deny list also prevents users from sharing individual SharePoint Online and OneDrive files with users in fabrikam.com.
opzione_a: While the deny list is in place, you can also configure an allow list that contains contoso.com so that invitations to contoso.com are explicitly permitted.
opzione_b: If you switch the setting to "Allow invitations only to the specified domains (most restrictive)", the existing deny list configuration is discarded.
opzione_c: The deny list also prevents users from sharing individual SharePoint Online and OneDrive files with users in fabrikam.com.
spiegazione: Statement 1 - No: Microsoft Learn is explicit that you can create either an allow list or a block list, but you can't set up both types of lists. By default, whatever domains are not in the allow list are on the block list, and vice versa. Only one policy per organization is supported; you can update the policy to include more domains, or delete the policy to create a new one. Statement 2 - Yes: The "Switch from allow list to block list and vice versa" section states that switching from one policy to another discards the existing policy configuration, which is why the documentation advises backing up the details of your configuration before you perform the switch. Statement 3 - No: This list works independently from the OneDrive and SharePoint Online allow/block lists. To restrict individual file sharing in SharePoint Online you must set up a separate allow or block list for OneDrive and SharePoint Online. Also note that the list does not apply to external users who have already redeemed their invitation - it is enforced only from the time it is set up, although a pending invitation whose domain becomes blocked will fail at redemption.
tags: allow list,block list,collaboration restrictions,b2b invitations,external collaboration settings

sotto_argomento: Manage external users
domanda: In the external collaboration settings of your Microsoft Entra tenant, Guest invite settings is set to "Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users". A project coordinator named Alena must be able to invite external partners for B2B collaboration. Alena must not be able to manage user accounts or any other directory objects. Which role should you assign to Alena?
opzione_a: Guest Inviter
opzione_b: User Administrator
opzione_c: External Identity Provider Administrator
opzione_d: Global Administrator
spiegazione: Correct: The Guest Inviter role gives individual users the ability to invite guests without assigning them a higher-privilege administrator role. Users with the Guest Inviter role can invite guests even when "Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users" is selected. B is wrong: User Administrator is the other role that permits inviting guests under that setting, but it additionally grants broad rights to create, delete and manage user accounts and reset passwords, so it violates the least-privilege requirement. C is wrong: External Identity Provider Administrator manages identity provider configuration and external collaboration settings; it is not the least-privileged role for merely sending invitations, and it is not one of the two roles that the "specific admin roles" option refers to. D is wrong: Global Administrator is the most privileged role in the tenant and Microsoft explicitly recommends limiting it to emergency scenarios.
tags: b2b collaboration,guest inviter,external collaboration settings,guest invite settings,least privilege

sotto_argomento: Manage external users
domanda: A new Microsoft Entra tenant was created for Litware, Inc. No administrator has modified the external collaboration settings since the tenant was created. A security reviewer asks you what B2B collaboration guest users are currently able to see in the directory. Which Guest user access level is in effect?
opzione_a: Guest users have the same access as members (most inclusive)
opzione_b: Guest users have limited access to properties and memberships of directory objects
opzione_c: Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects (most restrictive)
opzione_d: Guest users have no access to any directory data until an administrator assigns them a directory role
spiegazione: Correct: "Guest users have limited access to properties and memberships of directory objects" is flagged as (Default) in the Guest user access list in Microsoft Learn. It blocks guests from certain directory tasks such as enumerating users, groups, or other directory resources, while still allowing guests to see the membership of all non-hidden groups. A is wrong: this option gives guests the same access to Microsoft Entra resources and directory data as member users, and it is not the default - it must be selected explicitly. C is wrong: this is the most restrictive option, under which guests can access only their own profiles; it is also not the default and must be selected explicitly. D is wrong: no such option exists; guests always receive a default set of permissions when they are added to the directory, and a directory role assignment is not a prerequisite for any directory read access.
tags: guest permissions,external collaboration settings,guest user access,default permissions,b2b

sotto_argomento: Manage external users
domanda: Your Microsoft Entra tenant uses the email one-time passcode feature for B2B collaboration guests who cannot be authenticated by any other identity provider. A guest reports that the passcode she received stopped working before she could use it, and a different guest reports being asked for a new passcode the following morning. Which statement correctly describes the built-in lifetimes of email one-time passcode authentication?
opzione_a: One-time passcodes are valid for 30 minutes, and guest user sessions expire after 24 hours.
opzione_b: One-time passcodes are valid for 5 minutes, and guest user sessions expire after 90 days.
opzione_c: One-time passcodes are valid for 60 minutes, and guest user sessions expire after 14 days.
opzione_d: One-time passcodes are valid for 30 days, and guest user sessions never expire until the guest account is deleted.
spiegazione: Correct: Microsoft Learn states that one-time passcodes are valid for 30 minutes, after which that specific passcode is no longer valid and the user must request a new one, and that user sessions expire after 24 hours, at which point the guest receives a new passcode when they access the resource. B, C and D are wrong: they use plausible-looking but incorrect lifetimes. The 90-day and 14-day values are commonly confused with sign-in and refresh-token lifetimes elsewhere in Microsoft Entra ID, and no email one-time passcode session is unlimited - session expiration is deliberate added security for cases where a guest leaves their company or no longer needs access. Neither lifetime is configurable by the tenant administrator.
tags: email one-time passcode,b2b collaboration,guest authentication,otp,external id

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: At Litware, a user account is synchronized from Windows Server Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID by using Microsoft Entra Connect. Group-based license assignment for the user fails because the Usage location property is empty. The on-premises identity team confirms that the user's identity, contact, and job attributes must be changed on-premises. You must populate Usage location for the user with the least administrative effort. What should you do?
opzione_a: Set the Usage location property on the user directly in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
opzione_b: Populate the country attribute on the user object in Windows Server Active Directory and wait for the next synchronization cycle.
opzione_c: Create a custom inbound synchronization rule in Microsoft Entra Connect that maps an on-premises attribute to usageLocation.
opzione_d: Exclude the user's organizational unit from synchronization so that the account becomes cloud-only, and then set Usage location.
spiegazione: Correct: Set Usage location directly in the Microsoft Entra admin center. The documentation states that for users whose source of authority is Windows Server Active Directory you must use Windows Server Active Directory to update their identity, contact info, or job info; however, you can update their attributes directly in the Microsoft Entra admin center if you are updating Microsoft Entra ID attributes, such as Usage Location. Usage location is a Microsoft Entra ID attribute, so the on-premises source-of-authority restriction does not apply to it. Incorrect - Populate the country attribute on-premises: usageLocation is not synchronized from the on-premises country attribute by default, so this would not resolve the failure, and it also changes an attribute users may see. Incorrect - Create a custom synchronization rule: this can work but is far more administrative effort than editing an attribute that Microsoft Entra ID already allows you to edit directly, and custom sync rules add ongoing maintenance and upgrade risk. Incorrect - Exclude the OU to make the account cloud-only: this is a drastic change that breaks the hybrid identity model for that user and is unnecessary, since the attribute is directly editable in the cloud.
tags: microsoft entra id,usage location,microsoft entra connect,hybrid identity,user properties,licensing

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: Adventure Works uses group-based licensing. A Microsoft 365 E3 license is assigned to the group GRP-Sales and also to the group GRP-Marketing. Several users are transferring from Sales to Marketing. You must move the users between the two groups so that they do not lose access to licensed services at any point during the move. What should you do?
opzione_a: Remove the users from GRP-Sales, and then add them to GRP-Marketing.
opzione_b: Add the users to GRP-Marketing, confirm that the new license has been applied on each user's Licenses page, and then remove them from GRP-Sales.
opzione_c: Remove the users from GRP-Sales and add them to GRP-Marketing within the same bulk membership operation.
opzione_d: Assign a Microsoft 365 E3 license directly to each user, remove them from GRP-Sales, and then add them to GRP-Marketing.
spiegazione: Correct: Add to the destination group first, confirm the license applied, then remove from the source group. The documentation states that when you move a user from one licensed group to another the order of operations matters, and prescribes exactly this sequence to move a user between licensed groups without service interruption. Incorrect - Remove first, then add: this is the documented failure mode. If you remove the user from the source group first, the user is unlicensed until group-based licensing finishes processing the new group's assignment, and processing time varies by tenant size and load. Incorrect - Same bulk operation: bundling both changes into one operation does not guarantee ordering or immediate processing. Group-based licensing processes membership changes asynchronously, so the user can still be left temporarily unlicensed. Incorrect - Assign a direct license first: this does technically mask the gap, but it is not the documented approach and it creates a direct license assignment on every user that must later be cleaned up, defeating the purpose of group-based licensing and risking double consumption.
tags: microsoft entra id,group-based licensing,group membership,service interruption,license processing

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: Some Microsoft services are not available in every country or region. Because of this, one property on a Microsoft Entra user account must be populated before a Microsoft 365 license can be assigned to that user. Which property must be set?
opzione_a: Office location
opzione_b: Usage location
opzione_c: Country or region
opzione_d: Preferred data location
spiegazione: Correct: Usage location. The documentation states that because some Microsoft services aren't available in all locations, the administrator must specify the user's location setting before a license can be assigned to that user. Usage location is the attribute that licensing evaluates to determine which services may be enabled for the user. For group-based licensing, any users without a specific location inherit the location of the tenant. Incorrect - Office location: this is a descriptive profile/job attribute shown on the user's profile card; it has no effect on license assignment or service eligibility. Incorrect - Country or region: this is a contact/address attribute of the user profile. It is a common misconception that it drives licensing, but license assignment specifically evaluates Usage location, and the two are separate attributes that can hold different values. Incorrect - Preferred data location: this attribute is used with Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo to control the geography in which a user's data is stored at rest. It does not determine whether a license can be assigned.
tags: microsoft entra id,licensing,usage location,user properties,group-based licensing

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: After assigning a product license to a group, an administrator opens the product details page in the Microsoft 365 admin center and reviews the Errors & issues tab, which lists members who have license assignment problems. Which of the following are documented causes of group license assignment errors? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_a: There are not enough available licenses in the subscription for every member of the group.
opzione_b: The assignment includes service plans that conflict and cannot be assigned to the same user.
opzione_c: Two members of the group have duplicate proxy addresses.
opzione_d: The group contains a nested group whose members push the total membership above the purchased license count.
opzione_e: One of the group members has a disabled sign-in status.
spiegazione: Correct: insufficient licenses, conflicting service plans, and duplicate proxy addresses. The documentation lists the group license error types as insufficient licenses, conflicting service plans, missing dependencies, proxy address issues, and usage location problems. Insufficient licenses occurs when the subscription does not have enough units for every member; conflicting service plans occurs when two service plans in the assignment cannot coexist on the same user; proxy address issues occur when more than one object carries the same proxy address, which blocks the Exchange-related service plan. Incorrect - Nested group members pushing membership above the license count: nested group members are never processed by group-based licensing at all, since only first-level members are assigned licenses. They therefore cannot consume licenses or generate this error. Incorrect - A member with a disabled sign-in status: account enablement is unrelated to license assignment. Disabled accounts can still hold licenses and do not appear as a license assignment error.
tags: microsoft entra id,group-based licensing,license conflicts,service plans,proxy address,troubleshooting

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: Contoso assigns a Microsoft 365 E3 license to a security group named GRP-All by using group-based licensing. GRP-All has 200 users as direct members and also contains a nested security group named GRP-Contractors, which has 40 users as members. None of the 40 contractors are direct members of GRP-All. Which users are assigned the Microsoft 365 E3 license?
opzione_a: Only the 200 direct members of GRP-All
opzione_b: All 240 users, because nested group membership is evaluated transitively
opzione_c: Only the 40 members of GRP-Contractors
opzione_d: No users, because assigning a license to a group that contains a nested group is blocked
spiegazione: Correct: Only the 200 direct members of GRP-All. The documentation states that group-based licensing doesn't currently support nested groups, and that if you assign licenses to a nested group, only users in the first-level group are assigned licenses. The 40 contractors are members of the nested child group, not first-level members of GRP-All, so they receive nothing. Incorrect - All 240 users: this is the classic misconception. Transitive/nested evaluation is used by many Microsoft Entra features (for example, app assignment scenarios and some access checks), but group-based licensing explicitly does not process nested groups. Incorrect - Only the 40 members of GRP-Contractors: the license is assigned to GRP-All, and processing works downward to first-level members only; it is never restricted to the nested group alone. Incorrect - No users: the assignment is not blocked. It succeeds and licenses the first-level members; the nested members are simply ignored, which is why this limitation is easy to miss.
tags: microsoft entra id,group-based licensing,nested groups,security group,limitations

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: Woodgrove Bank manages product licenses for thousands of users by using group-based licensing in the Microsoft 365 admin center. An administrator is planning a bulk assignment and needs to account for the documented limitations of the feature. Select the correct value for each statement.
opzione_a: Maximum number of groups you can assign licenses to at a time: [10 | 20 | 50]
opzione_b: Maximum number of users the Reprocess action attempts to reprocess at a time: [20 | 100 | 999]
opzione_c: Number of users displayed at a time in the paginated lists of successful and unsuccessful assignments: [100 | 500 | 999]
spiegazione: Correct values are 20, 20, and 999. The documented limitations of group-based licensing in the Microsoft 365 admin center state that you can assign licenses to a maximum of 20 groups at a time; that when you select Reprocess to resolve issues with group license assignment, the feature attempts to reprocess licenses up to a maximum of 20 users at a time; and that the lists of users who were and who weren't successfully assigned licenses are paginated lists that display 999 users at a time, requiring you to scroll to the bottom to load the next set. Incorrect - 10 or 50 groups: these are plausible-looking round numbers but the documented ceiling is 20 groups per assignment operation. Incorrect - 100 or 999 users for Reprocess: Reprocess is capped at 20 users per action, not 999; 999 is the pagination size of the result lists, which is the value this distractor deliberately confuses it with. Incorrect - 100 or 500 users per page: the documented pagination size is 999.
tags: microsoft entra id,group-based licensing,limits,reprocess,microsoft 365 admin center

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: Which Microsoft Graph PowerShell cmdlet returns the members of a group who failed to receive a license through group-based licensing, so that you can investigate the cause?
opzione_a: Get-MgGroupMember
opzione_b: Get-MgGroupMemberWithLicenseError
opzione_c: Get-MgSubscribedSku
opzione_d: Set-MgGroupLicense
spiegazione: Correct: Get-MgGroupMemberWithLicenseError. This cmdlet is documented specifically for identifying the members of a group who are in an error state for group-based license assignment, which is the first step in troubleshooting problems such as insufficient licenses or conflicting service plans. Incorrect - Get-MgGroupMember: this returns all members of the group without any filtering on license assignment state, so it does not isolate the users in error. Incorrect - Get-MgSubscribedSku: this returns the subscribed SKUs in the tenant, including consumed and enabled unit counts. It is useful for checking how many licenses remain, but it reports at the tenant/SKU level and does not identify which group members failed. Incorrect - Set-MgGroupLicense: this is a write cmdlet used to add or remove license assignments on a group; it configures group-based licensing rather than reporting errors.
tags: microsoft entra id,group-based licensing,microsoft graph powershell,troubleshooting,license errors

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: Proseware uses group-based licensing. A Microsoft 365 E3 product license is assigned to a security group named GRP-Engineering. GRP-Engineering contains 500 direct user members and one nested security group named GRP-Interns that contains 25 users who are not direct members of GRP-Engineering. All users have a Usage location configured. Evaluate each of the following statements and indicate whether it is true. 1) When a new user is added as a direct member of GRP-Engineering, Microsoft Entra ID automatically assigns the Microsoft 365 E3 license to that user. 2) When a user is removed from GRP-Engineering, Microsoft Entra ID removes the license assignment that the user inherited from the group. 3) The 25 users in GRP-Interns are assigned the Microsoft 365 E3 license because their group is a member of GRP-Engineering.
opzione_a: When a new user is added as a direct member of GRP-Engineering, Microsoft Entra ID automatically assigns the Microsoft 365 E3 license to that user.
opzione_b: When a user is removed from GRP-Engineering, Microsoft Entra ID removes the license assignment that the user inherited from the group.
opzione_c: The 25 users in GRP-Interns are assigned the Microsoft 365 E3 license because their group is a member of GRP-Engineering.
spiegazione: Statement 1 - Yes: the documentation states that Microsoft Entra users who join a licensed group are automatically assigned the appropriate licenses, which is the core value of group-based licensing and removes the need for scripts to license joiners. Statement 2 - Yes: the documentation states that when users leave the group, Microsoft Entra ID removes their license assignments. Note this only reclaims the license inherited from the group; a license that was also assigned directly to the user would remain and must be removed separately. Statement 3 - No: group-based licensing doesn't currently support nested groups. If you assign licenses to a group, only users in the first-level group are assigned licenses, so the 25 members of the nested GRP-Interns receive nothing and would need to be direct members of GRP-Engineering, or have the license assigned to GRP-Interns itself.
tags: microsoft entra id,group-based licensing,nested groups,license inheritance,group membership

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: You are delegating permissions at Northwind Traders so that helpdesk staff can assign product licenses to groups in the Microsoft 365 admin center, without granting Global Administrator. Which built-in roles allow a user to assign licenses to a group? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
opzione_a: Groups Administrator
opzione_b: License Administrator
opzione_c: User Administrator
opzione_d: Billing Administrator
opzione_e: Helpdesk Administrator
spiegazione: Correct: Groups Administrator, License Administrator, and User Administrator. The documentation states that you must be at least a Groups Administrator, License Administrator, or User Administrator to assign licenses to a group. Incorrect - Billing Administrator: this role manages purchases, subscriptions, invoices and payment methods. It can buy licenses for the tenant, but purchasing licenses is not the same as assigning them to users or groups, which is the classic confusion this option tests. Incorrect - Helpdesk Administrator: this role is scoped to resetting passwords and managing sign-in and service requests for non-administrator users. It is not among the roles documented for license assignment.

sotto_argomento: Manage resource groups
domanda: Contoso is consolidating workloads and needs to move a virtual machine and its dependent resources from a subscription named Sub-Legacy to a subscription named Sub-Corp. You must ensure the move operation succeeds on the first attempt. Which conditions must be satisfied before you start the move? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_a: Both the source and the destination subscriptions must exist within the same Microsoft Entra tenant.
opzione_b: The destination subscription must be registered for the resource provider of each resource type being moved.
opzione_c: The resource and its dependent resources must be located in the same resource group and must be moved together in the same operation.
opzione_d: The source resource group and the destination resource group must be created in the same Azure region.
opzione_e: All existing Azure role assignments on the moved resources are automatically re-created in the destination subscription, so no post-move action is required.
spiegazione: Correct: a, b, c. The Microsoft Learn checklist for moving resources states that (a) the source and destination subscriptions must exist within the same Microsoft Entra tenant - if the tenant IDs differ you must first transfer billing ownership or associate the subscription with the target tenant; (b) the destination subscription must be registered for the resource provider of the resource you're moving, otherwise you receive an error stating the subscription isn't registered for a resource type; and (c) for a move across subscriptions, the resource and its dependent resources must be located in the same resource group and be moved together - a VM with managed disks requires the VM, the disks, and the other dependent resources to move in one operation, otherwise you get MissingMoveDependentResources. Wrong: d - there is no requirement that the source and destination resource groups share a region. Moving a resource only changes its associated resource group and does not alter the physical region of the resource; a region change requires Azure Resource Mover instead. Wrong: e - the opposite is documented: if you move a resource with an active Azure role assignment, the role assignment does not move and becomes orphaned. You must create the role assignment again after the move, and Microsoft recommends removing the orphaned assignment before the move.
tags: move resources, subscription move, entra tenant, resource provider, dependent resources, rbac

sotto_argomento: Manage resource groups
domanda: A colleague starts a move operation to relocate several virtual machines from a resource group named RG-Prod to a resource group named RG-Archive in the same subscription. While the move is running, another engineer reports that she cannot resize a virtual machine that is not part of the move but resides in RG-Prod. What is the expected behavior during a resource move operation?
opzione_a: Both the source and the destination resource groups are locked, so resources in them cannot be created, deleted, or updated, but existing resources keep running without downtime.
opzione_b: Only the source resource group is locked; the destination resource group remains fully writable until the move completes.
opzione_c: The resources included in the move are automatically stopped and deallocated for the duration of the move, and other resources in the resource group are unaffected.
opzione_d: A read-only lock is automatically applied at the subscription scope, blocking all write operations across every resource group in the subscription.
spiegazione: Correct: a. Microsoft Learn states that during the move operation both the source and target resource groups are locked, so you cannot create, delete, or update resources within these resource groups while the move is in progress; however, existing resources remain fully operational and services relying on them experience no downtime. The lock can last up to four hours, although most moves finish sooner. This is exactly why resizing a VM in RG-Prod fails. Wrong: b - the lock is applied to both the source and the destination resource groups, not just the source, and neither can participate in another move simultaneously. Wrong: c - moving a resource does not stop or deallocate it; the documentation is explicit that the VM continues to operate normally and dependent services see no downtime. Also, the lock affects the whole resource group, not only the resources being moved. Wrong: d - the automatic lock is scoped to the two resource groups involved, not to the entire subscription. (Separately, a manually created read-only lock on the source or destination blocks the move from happening at all.)
tags: move resources, resource group, lock, azure resource manager, troubleshooting

sotto_argomento: Manage resource groups
domanda: During a design review, a colleague asks why Azure requires you to select a location when you create a resource group, given that the resources inside the group can be deployed to entirely different regions. Which statement correctly explains the purpose of the resource group location?
opzione_a: The location determines the region where the resource group stores the metadata about its resources.
opzione_b: The location restricts the resources in the resource group to that region only.
opzione_c: The location determines the region whose meter rates are used to bill all resources in the resource group.
opzione_d: The location defines the paired region to which Azure automatically replicates all resources in the resource group for disaster recovery.
spiegazione: Correct: a. Microsoft Learn states that the resource group stores metadata about its resources, so specifying a location for the resource group specifies where that metadata is stored.
